meta.note: Hand-authored O2C operational pattern library — the domains the AR-centric library never covered: pricing & rebates, logistics & freight, direct store delivery, returns & returnable assets, and master data / channels / controls. Same shape as an xlsx-derived pattern; priorityRank, featureSlug and hitlGates are re-derived at build time. Merged into patterns.json by build_patterns.py.
meta.voice: Written in the first person of the operator who owns the mission — the thing a 20-year practitioner notices before the report does.

patterns.name: Condition Record Overlap
patterns.mentalModel: Two valid condition records can cover the same customer/material at the same time, and SAP will silently pick the most specific one — which is almost never the one I intended. I have watched a national price increase land while a forgotten customer-specific record from a two-year-old promotion kept winning the access sequence. Nobody raises a ticket, because the order prices successfully. Let me pull KONH validity windows per access-sequence key and find the ones that overlap; wherever they do, I want to know which record actually won on the last hundred orders and what that cost per case.

sap: KONH (KSCHL, DATAB, DATBI, KNUMH) - condition header validity windows
KONP (KBETR, KONWA) - condition rate per record
PRCD_ELEMENTS / KONV (KNUMH, KWERT) - which record actually priced the document
T682I - access sequence, to know which key combination outranks which

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: For each access-sequence key combination, self-join KONH to itself on the same key and test whether the DATAB-DATBI windows intersect, then join PRCD_ELEMENTS to see which KNUMH actually priced recent documents.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Condition_Record_Created, Validity_Window_Overlap_Begins and Applied_On_Document events to expose the date at which the wrong record began winning.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT a.KNUMH, b.KNUMH, SUM(v.KWERT) AS priced_value
FROM KONH a JOIN KONH b ON a.key_combo = b.key_combo AND a.KNUMH <> b.KNUMH
  AND a.DATAB <= b.DATBI AND b.DATAB <= a.DATBI
JOIN PRCD_ELEMENTS v ON v.KNUMH = b.KNUMH
WHERE b.KBETR < a.KBETR -> flag Overlap_Losing_Margin

branchingDAG.condition: IF Overlap_Exists AND Margin_Delta_Per_Case < 0.5% AND Documents_Priced < 20

branchingDAG.hitl: Pricing Operations Lead approves condition record closure
Commercial Finance approves cross-org price correction

patterns.name: Open-Ended Validity Drift
patterns.mentalModel: A promotional condition entered with an end date of 31.12.9999 is not a promotion, it is a permanent price cut that nobody signed off. The person who keyed it meant to come back and close it. They never do. I check every condition record whose validity end is beyond the horizon and whose condition type is a discount, then ask when the underlying deal actually expired — the gap between those two dates, multiplied by volume, is pure unbudgeted spend.

sap: KONH (DATBI, KSCHL, ERDAT, ERNAM) - end date, type and who created it
KONP (KBETR) - the discount rate still running
VBRP (FKIMG, NETWR) - volume invoiced under the record since deal expiry
CDHDR/CDPOS (KONH) - change history on the validity date
oracle: OZF_OFFERS (END_DATE, STATUS_CODE) [Fusion] - the offer the line was meant to serve

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Filter KONH to discount condition types with DATBI >= 9999-12-31, join to the source deal or offer record to recover the intended end date, then join VBRP for volume invoiced after that date.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Deal_Expiry_Date against Condition_Still_Active and Invoice_Discounted events to measure the unbudgeted tail.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT h.KNUMH, h.KSCHL, h.ERNAM, SUM(p.NETWR * k.KBETR/100) AS unbudgeted_spend
FROM KONH h JOIN KONP k USING(KNUMH) JOIN VBRP p ON p.KNUMH = h.KNUMH
WHERE h.DATBI >= '99991231' AND h.KSCHL IN (discount_types)
  AND p.FKDAT > deal_expiry -> flag Perpetual_Discount

branchingDAG.hitl: Pricing Operations Lead approves record closure and recovery assessment
OTC Controls Lead approves user-level access review

patterns.name: Deal Sheet Divergence
patterns.mentalModel: The contract says ten percent. The condition record says twelve. Somebody fat-fingered it eighteen months ago and every invoice since has been two points light. This is the most boring and most expensive defect in pricing, because it never errors — it just quietly underbills. I reconcile the signed commercial terms line by line against the live condition records and treat any variance beyond rounding as a recoverable, not a correction.

sap: KONA (KNUMA, BOART, KUNNR) - the agreement as signed
KONP (KBETR) - the rate actually configured
WCOCO / WCOCOH (S/4 condition contract header and conditions)
VBRP (NETWR, FKIMG) - value invoiced under the diverging rate

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Join the agreement or contract terms to the executing condition record on agreement number and compare the negotiated rate to the configured rate, then value the delta against invoiced volume.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Contract_Signed, Condition_Configured and Invoice_Priced events to date the divergence and size the exposure since.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT a.KNUMA, a.agreed_rate, k.KBETR AS configured_rate,
       SUM(p.NETWR) * ABS(a.agreed_rate - k.KBETR)/100 AS exposure
FROM KONA a JOIN KONP k USING(KNUMA) JOIN VBRP p USING(KNUMA)
WHERE ABS(a.agreed_rate - k.KBETR) > 0.05 -> flag Deal_Divergence

branchingDAG.hitl: Commercial Finance approves retrospective recovery approach
Commercial Finance approves proactive customer credit

patterns.name: Accrual Attainment Drift
patterns.mentalModel: We accrue rebate at the rate we expect the customer to earn. If they are tracking to a higher tier than the accrual assumes, the true-up at settlement is a P&L shock in the worst quarter to take one. I run attainment-to-date against the tier table every month and compare the implied final rate to the rate we are actually accruing at. A widening gap in either direction is a controllable warning, not a year-end surprise.

sap: KONA (KNUMA, BOART) - rebate agreement and type
KOTE / rebate scales - the tier table and thresholds
VBOX / S/4 condition contract settlement index - volume accumulated to date
BSEG (HKONT, DMBTR) - accrual actually posted

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Accumulate qualifying volume per agreement to date, resolve the tier that volume implies at period end, and compare the implied rate to the rate underlying the posted accrual.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Monthly_Attainment, Implied_Tier_Change and Accrual_Posted events to expose the month the accrual stopped tracking reality.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT a.KNUMA, implied_tier_rate, accrued_rate,
       (implied_tier_rate - accrued_rate) * ytd_volume AS true_up_exposure
FROM KONA a JOIN attainment USING(KNUMA) JOIN accrual USING(KNUMA)
WHERE ABS(implied_tier_rate - accrued_rate) >= 1.0 -> flag Accrual_Drift

branchingDAG.hitl: Financial Controller approves accrual rate change
Financial Controller approves catch-up provision at close

patterns.name: Retro Tier Reach-Back
patterns.mentalModel: A customer crosses a volume threshold in the last week of the period and then claims the higher rate on everything they bought all year. If the contract says the tier applies prospectively, that claim is worth nothing — but it will be paid unless somebody reads the clause. I watch for tier crossings late in the period and check the retroactivity wording before the settlement run goes anywhere near it.

sap: KONA (KNUMA) + rebate scale - tier thresholds and retroactivity flag
VBOX - period volume accumulation by date
KONB / settlement documents - what the settlement proposes to pay
VBRK (FKDAT) - the invoice dates the claim reaches back over

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Detect the date a customer crosses a tier threshold, read the agreement retroactivity flag, and compare the settlement basis to the volume that occurred after the crossing.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Threshold_Crossing_Date, Claim_Basis_Start_Date and Settlement_Proposed events to expose claims that reach back before entitlement began.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT c.KNUMA, crossing_date, claim_basis_start,
       SUM(pre_crossing_volume * tier_delta) AS over_claim
FROM claims c JOIN KONA a USING(KNUMA)
WHERE a.retroactive_flag = 'N' AND claim_basis_start < crossing_date -> flag Reach_Back

branchingDAG.condition: ELSE IF Retroactive_Flag = N AND Over_Claim >= 25K
branchingDAG.hitl: Contract & Rebates Operations Lead approves settlement recalculation
Commercial Finance approves challenge to period-end loading

patterns.name: Buying Group Double Dip
patterns.mentalModel: In any buying-group or multi-company-code structure the same case of product can be claimed twice — once by the member who bought it and once by the group that aggregates it. Each claim looks clean in isolation because they sit in different agreements. I have to net them at the volume level, not the claim level. Any case number that appears under both a member agreement and a group agreement in the same period is being paid for twice.

sap: KNVH (HITYP, HKUNNR) - customer hierarchy, member to group
KONA (KNUMA, KUNNR) - agreements at both member and group level
VBRP (VGBEL, FKIMG) - the invoiced volume both claims rest on
VBOX - rebate index showing which agreements captured the same billing doc
oracle: OZF_CLAIMS_ALL (CUST_ACCOUNT_ID, CLAIM_AMOUNT) [Fusion] - claims at both levels

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Resolve each billing document to both its member and its hierarchy parent, then test whether rebate accrual or settlement exists against the same document under more than one agreement.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Billing_Doc_Created, Member_Claim_Applied and Group_Claim_Applied to expose documents captured twice in one period.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT p.VBELN, COUNT(DISTINCT b.KNUMA) AS agreements, SUM(b.rebate_value) AS paid
FROM VBRP p JOIN VBOX b ON b.VBELN = p.VBELN
JOIN KNVH h ON h.KUNNR = p.KUNAG
GROUP BY p.VBELN HAVING agreements > 1 -> flag Double_Dip

branchingDAG.hitl: Contract & Rebates Operations Lead approves claim netting
Commercial Finance approves agreement restructure and recovery claim

patterns.name: Off-Invoice On-Accrual Overlap
patterns.mentalModel: The same allowance can be granted twice in two different currencies of the P&L — once as an off-invoice discount that reduces net price, and once as an accrued rebate that hits trade spend. Gross-to-net looks fine on either report alone. I reconcile the condition types applied on the invoice against the accrual conditions on the same document; where a discount and an accrual describe the same commercial promise, one of them is double-counted.

sap: PRCD_ELEMENTS / KONV (KSCHL, KWERT) - all condition types on the billing document
T685 (KSCHL, KRECH) - condition type semantics: discount vs accrual
KONA (BOART) - the agreement behind the accrual
VBRP (NETWR, KZWI1..KZWI6) - subtotal buckets carrying gross-to-net
oracle: OZF_FUNDS_UTILIZED_ALL_B [Fusion] - accrual utilisation against the same order

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: For each billing document, classify every applied condition type as off-invoice discount or accrual, then group by the commercial promise they trace to and flag documents carrying both.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Discount_Applied and Accrual_Posted events against a single billing document to expose the same promise funded twice.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT v.VBELN, SUM(CASE WHEN t.type='discount' THEN v.KWERT END) AS off_invoice,
       SUM(CASE WHEN t.type='accrual' THEN v.KWERT END) AS accrued
FROM PRCD_ELEMENTS v JOIN T685 t USING(KSCHL)
GROUP BY v.VBELN HAVING off_invoice IS NOT NULL AND accrued IS NOT NULL
  AND same_promise = 1 -> flag Overlap

branchingDAG.hitl: Commercial Finance approves gross-to-net restatement
Financial Controller approves prior-period gross-to-net adjustment

patterns.name: Dormant Agreement Accrual
patterns.mentalModel: A rebate agreement that is still open against a customer who stopped buying eight months ago is a liability nobody is looking at. It either accrues on nothing and sits stale on the balance sheet, or worse, it stays live for the day that customer returns and claims against terms we would never sign today. I age every open agreement by last qualifying transaction and force a decision on anything dormant beyond two settlement cycles.

sap: KONA (KNUMA, BOSTA, DATBI) - agreement status and validity
VBOX - last qualifying billing document per agreement
BSEG (HKONT, DMBTR) - accrual balance still carried
KNB1 / VBAK - whether the customer is still trading at all

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Age each open agreement by the date of its last qualifying billing document and join to the carried accrual balance and the customer's overall trading activity.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Last_Qualifying_Transaction, Settlement_Cycles_Elapsed and Accrual_Balance_Carried to expose agreements that are open but inert.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT a.KNUMA, MAX(b.FKDAT) AS last_activity, bal.DMBTR AS carried_accrual
FROM KONA a LEFT JOIN VBOX b USING(KNUMA) JOIN accrual_bal bal USING(KNUMA)
WHERE a.BOSTA = 'open' AND MONTHS_BETWEEN(today, MAX(b.FKDAT)) >= 6
  -> flag Dormant_Agreement

branchingDAG.condition: IF Dormant < 2 settlement cycles AND Customer_Still_Trading
ELSE IF Dormant >= 2 cycles AND Carried_Accrual >= 25K
branchingDAG.hitl: Financial Controller approves accrual release
Commercial Finance approves permanent agreement closure

patterns.name: Sub-Threshold Override Cluster
patterns.mentalModel: Every pricing approval matrix has a number in it, and every number creates a shadow just underneath. When one user grants manual price overrides to the same customer group again and again, each a whisker below their approval limit, that is not commercial judgement — that is someone who has learned where the control sits. I cluster overrides by user, customer and distance-to-threshold; a tight cluster just under the line is the signal, not the individual override.

sap: PRCD_ELEMENTS / KONV (KSCHL, KWERT, KMANU) - manually entered condition values
VBAP (VBELN, POSNR, NETWR) - the order line overridden
CDHDR/CDPOS (USERNAME, UDATE) - who changed the price and when
T685A - the approval threshold the override sits under

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Filter condition values flagged as manually entered, join the change document to recover the user, and compute each override's distance below the user's approval threshold.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Override_Events per user and customer group and measure the dispersion of distance-to-threshold across them.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT c.USERNAME, v.KUNNR, COUNT(*) AS overrides,
       AVG(threshold - override_pct) AS avg_gap, STDDEV(threshold - override_pct) AS spread
FROM KONV v JOIN CDPOS c USING(VBELN)
WHERE v.KMANU = 'X' GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING overrides >= 5 AND avg_gap < 1.0 AND spread < 0.4 -> flag Shadow_Cluster

branchingDAG.hitl: OTC Controls Lead approves enhanced approval requirement
Internal Audit approves segregation-of-duties investigation

patterns.name: Settlement Without Claim Proof
patterns.mentalModel: A settlement run will happily pay a rebate that has no claim document behind it, or pay against a claim that was already settled last quarter. The run is doing exactly what it was told. My job is to check the evidence chain before the money leaves: every settlement line should trace to a claim, every claim to a qualifying volume, and no claim should appear in two settlement runs.

sap: KONB / settlement document - what the run proposes to pay
KONA (KNUMA) - the agreement authorising it
VBOX - the qualifying volume behind the claim
BKPF/BSEG - prior settlement postings against the same agreement period
oracle: OZF_CLAIMS_ALL (CLAIM_NUMBER, STATUS_CODE) [Fusion] - claim and its state

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Join every proposed settlement line back to its claim, the claim back to qualifying volume, and check prior postings for the same agreement and period.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Claim_Raised, Volume_Qualified and Settlement_Posted events to expose settlements with a broken or repeated evidence chain.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT s.settlement_id, s.KNUMA, s.amount,
       CASE WHEN c.claim_id IS NULL THEN 'no_claim'
            WHEN prior.settlement_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'already_settled' END AS defect
FROM settlements s LEFT JOIN claims c USING(claim_id)
LEFT JOIN settlements prior ON prior.claim_id = s.claim_id AND prior.id <> s.id
WHERE defect IS NOT NULL -> flag Evidence_Break

branchingDAG.hitl: Contract & Rebates Operations Lead approves settlement hold
Financial Controller approves duplicate-settlement recovery

patterns.name: Delivery Date Washing
patterns.mentalModel: OTIF is measured against the confirmed date, so the cheapest way to fix OTIF is to change the confirmed date. I have seen a site run 97% on-time for a year while customers were escalating weekly, because the planner reconfirmed every at-risk delivery two days out. The give-away is in the change log, not the report: a delivery whose LFDAT was amended after the original date had already passed, or amended more than once, was never on time. I rebuild OTIF against the FIRST confirmed date and show both numbers side by side.

sap: LIKP (VBELN, LFDAT, WADAT_IST) - delivery header, planned and actual goods issue
CDHDR/CDPOS (OBJECTID=LIKP, FNAME='LFDAT') - every amendment to the promised date
VBEP (EDATU, ETENR) - original schedule line confirmation on the order
VBFA - order to delivery document flow

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Recover the first confirmed delivery date from the order schedule line and the change log, then recompute on-time against that date rather than the current LFDAT.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Original_Confirmation, Date_Amendment_Events and Actual_Goods_Issue to expose deliveries reconfirmed after the original date had lapsed.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT l.VBELN, first_confirmed, l.LFDAT AS current_promise, l.WADAT_IST,
       COUNT(c.CHANGENR) AS amendments
FROM LIKP l JOIN CDPOS c ON c.OBJECTID = l.VBELN AND c.FNAME = 'LFDAT'
GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
HAVING amendments >= 1 AND l.WADAT_IST > first_confirmed -> flag Date_Washed

branchingDAG.hitl: Logistics Operations Lead approves OTIF restatement
Customer Compliance Lead approves amendment-authority freeze

patterns.name: Partial Ship Padding
patterns.mentalModel: Split a late order into two deliveries and the first one ships on time. Line fill looks healthy, order fill quietly collapses, and the customer — who ordered one delivery — counts it as a miss and charges us for it. I measure OTIF at the order the customer placed, not at the delivery we chose to create, and I look for splits that appear within days of the promise date rather than at the point of picking.

sap: LIPS (VBELN, VGBEL, VGPOS, LFIMG) - delivery items back to their order line
VBAP (KWMENG) - originally ordered quantity
LIKP (LFDAT, ERDAT) - when each split delivery was created versus promised
VBFA - one order line fanning out to several deliveries

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Group deliveries by originating order line, count the splits, and compare the creation date of each split to the original promise date.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Order_Line_Confirmed, Split_Delivery_Created and Goods_Issue events to expose splits created inside the promise window.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT p.VGBEL, p.VGPOS, COUNT(DISTINCT p.VBELN) AS splits,
       MIN(k.ERDAT) AS first_split_created, a.promise_date
FROM LIPS p JOIN LIKP k USING(VBELN) JOIN VBAP a ON a.VBELN = p.VGBEL
GROUP BY 1,2,4 HAVING splits > 1 AND first_split_created >= promise_date - 3
  -> flag Padding_Split

branchingDAG.hitl: Logistics Operations Lead approves order-level OTIF reporting change
Customer Compliance Lead approves discretionary split block

patterns.name: Accessorial Creep
patterns.mentalModel: The linehaul rate is negotiated to the cent and then the invoice arrives with detention, redelivery, liftgate and a fuel adjustment nobody has ever seen the derivation of. Accessorials are where carriers recover the margin they conceded in the tender. I trend accessorial charges as a share of linehaul by carrier and lane; when that share drifts up while the rate card is flat, the rate card is not what we are actually paying.

sap: VFKP (FKPTY, NETWR) - freight cost items by cost type
VFKK (FKNUM, TPLST) - freight cost header and planning point
TVFT / freight condition types - which charges are linehaul vs accessorial
LFA1 (LIFNR) - carrier master

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Classify every freight cost item as linehaul or accessorial, then compute accessorial share of total spend per carrier and lane per month.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Monthly_Accessorial_Share per carrier-lane and test for a sustained upward trend against a flat contracted rate.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT k.TPLST AS lane, p.LIFNR, period,
       SUM(CASE WHEN t.class='accessorial' THEN p.NETWR END) /
       NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN t.class='linehaul' THEN p.NETWR END),0) AS acc_share
FROM VFKP p JOIN VFKK k USING(FKNUM) JOIN TVFT t USING(FKPTY)
GROUP BY 1,2,3 HAVING trend(acc_share) > 0 AND acc_share > 0.18 -> flag Creep

branchingDAG.hitl: Logistics Operations Lead approves carrier accessorial challenge
Procurement approves withholding of uncontracted accessorial charges

patterns.name: Lane Rate Divergence
patterns.mentalModel: A carrier bills a lane at a rate that is not the tariff we signed. It is rarely dramatic — eleven dollars a shipment on a lane we run four hundred times a month. Nobody disputes eleven dollars. I re-rate every settled shipment against the contracted tariff for its lane, weight break and service level, and I care about the aggregate variance, not the individual one.

sap: VFKP (NETWR, MENGE) - what we were billed per shipment
TVRO / lane and route master - origin, destination, service level
Contracted tariff tables (agreement rates by lane and weight break)
VTTK (SHTYP, TNDR_STATUS) - shipment type and tender status
oracle: OTM rate offering and rate record tables

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: For each settled shipment resolve lane, weight break and service level, look up the contracted rate, and compare to the billed amount.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Tender_Accepted, Shipment_Executed and Invoice_Settled to expose the point at which billed rate detached from contracted rate.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT lane, weight_break, service_level,
       SUM(billed_amount - contracted_rate * units) AS variance, COUNT(*) AS shipments
FROM settled_shipments JOIN tariff USING(lane, weight_break, service_level)
GROUP BY 1,2,3 HAVING ABS(variance) >= 25000 -> flag Rate_Divergence

branchingDAG.hitl: Logistics Operations Lead approves carrier claim and settlement suspension
Procurement approves contract rate-load audit

patterns.name: Fuel Index Lag Arbitrage
patterns.mentalModel: Fuel surcharge is meant to track a published index on a defined weekly lag. When diesel falls, a carrier that keeps applying last month's index is charging a surcharge the market no longer supports — and it only ever seems to lag in one direction. I recompute FSC from the published index for the correct week and compare it to what was billed, then test whether the error is symmetric. Asymmetric error is not an error.

sap: VFKP (FKPTY='FSC', NETWR) - fuel surcharge lines
VFKK (ERDAT) - settlement date, to resolve the applicable index week
Published fuel index reference table
Carrier agreement FSC schedule (lag weeks, peg, escalator)

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Resolve the index week each shipment should have used from the agreement lag rule, recompute the entitled surcharge, and difference it against what was billed.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Index_Published, Entitled_FSC and Billed_FSC events to expose systematic lag in the carrier's favour.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT carrier, period, SUM(billed_fsc - entitled_fsc) AS overbill,
       CORR(index_direction, billed_minus_entitled) AS asymmetry
FROM fsc_lines JOIN fuel_index USING(index_week)
GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING overbill > 0 AND asymmetry < -0.5 -> flag Lag_Arbitrage

branchingDAG.hitl: Logistics Operations Lead approves fuel surcharge recovery claim
Procurement approves contract breach review

patterns.name: Duplicate Freight Settlement
patterns.mentalModel: The same shipment can be paid twice when it appears on a carrier's individual invoice and again inside a consolidated weekly manifest, or when a corrected invoice is loaded without reversing the original. Freight settlement volume is high and unit values are low, which is exactly the environment duplicates survive in. I fingerprint each settlement on shipment reference, date and amount and look for the same freight event settled more than once.

sap: VFKK (FKNUM, REFNR) - freight settlement documents and their references
VFKP (NETWR) - settled amounts
RSEG/RBKP - the invoice verification postings behind them
VTTK (TKNUM) - the shipment the settlement claims to cover

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Fingerprint every freight settlement on carrier, shipment reference, service date and amount, then group to find fingerprints settled more than once without a reversal.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Shipment_Executed, First_Settlement and Subsequent_Settlement events, checking for an intervening credit.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT TKNUM, LIFNR, COUNT(*) AS settlements, SUM(NETWR) AS paid
FROM VFKK k JOIN VFKP p USING(FKNUM)
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM reversals r WHERE r.FKNUM = k.FKNUM)
GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING settlements > 1 -> flag Duplicate_Settlement

branchingDAG.hitl: Logistics Operations Lead approves carrier debit note
Financial Controller approves duplicate freight recovery

patterns.name: Proof-of-Delivery Gap
patterns.mentalModel: A shipment marked delivered with no signed POD behind it is a deduction waiting sixty days to happen. The warehouse closes the delivery, billing fires, and the first anyone hears of it is a short-pay citing non-receipt — by which time the driver is gone and the paperwork is unrecoverable. I check POD capture at the moment of goods issue, not at the moment of dispute, and I chase the gap while the evidence still exists.

sap: LIKP (VBELN, PDSTK, WADAT_IST) - POD status and actual goods issue
TVPOD / VBPOD - proof-of-delivery confirmation records
VBRK (VBELN, FKDAT) - the invoice raised against it
BSEG (BLART='DZ') - the short-pay that eventually lands

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Join delivered shipments to their POD confirmation record and flag deliveries invoiced without one, then age the gap against the customer's typical deduction lag.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Goods_Issue, POD_Capture_Expected, Invoice_Raised and Deduction_Received to expose the window in which evidence is still recoverable.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT l.VBELN, l.WADAT_IST, r.VBELN AS invoice, pod.confirm_date
FROM LIKP l JOIN VBRK r ON r.VGBEL = l.VBELN
LEFT JOIN VBPOD pod USING(VBELN)
WHERE l.PDSTK <> 'C' AND pod.confirm_date IS NULL
  AND l.WADAT_IST <= today - 5 -> flag POD_Gap

branchingDAG.condition: ELSE IF At_Risk_Value >= 50K AND Gap_Age > 10 days
branchingDAG.hitl: Disputes & Deductions Lead approves pre-emptive customer contact
Financial Controller approves loss booking and carrier chargeback

patterns.name: Incoterm Cost Leakage
patterns.mentalModel: The incoterm on the order decides who pays the freight. When the order says the customer collects but we ship it on our account, we have given away the freight and nobody notices because it lands in distribution cost, not in a credit note. I reconcile the incoterm on every order against who actually bore the freight cost on the shipment, customer by customer. Delivered-terms creep is one of the quietest margin leaks in the business.

sap: VBKD (INCO1, INCO2) - incoterm agreed on the sales order
VFKP (NETWR) - freight cost actually borne on the shipment
VBRP (KSCHL freight condition) - freight recovered on the invoice
LIKP (VSBED) - shipping conditions applied

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: For each shipment compare the incoterm's cost obligation to the party that actually bore the freight, and to the freight recovered on the invoice.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Incoterm_Agreed, Freight_Cost_Incurred and Freight_Recovered to expose shipments where obligation and payment diverge.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT d.KUNNR, d.INCO1, SUM(f.NETWR) AS freight_borne,
       SUM(r.freight_billed) AS freight_recovered
FROM VBKD d JOIN VFKP f USING(VBELN) LEFT JOIN VBRP r USING(VBELN)
WHERE d.INCO1 IN ('EXW','FCA') AND freight_borne > 0
GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING freight_borne - COALESCE(freight_recovered,0) > 0 -> flag Leakage

branchingDAG.hitl: Commercial Finance approves freight recovery approach
Global Process Owner approves incoterm master data correction

patterns.name: Screening Bypass Window
patterns.mentalModel: Denied-party screening has to happen before the goods move, and the result has to be current. The dangerous case is not the order that fails screening — it is the order released in the window between a stale screening result and the re-screen that never ran, or released manually while the block was pending. This is the one exposure in my function that is not measured in dollars. I check every export goods issue against a screening result that was valid at that moment, not merely present.

sap: /SAPSLL/ GTS screening result tables - party screening status and timestamp
VBAK (VBELN, VKORG) + LIKP (WADAT_IST) - the order and when it actually shipped
CDHDR/CDPOS - manual release of a compliance block and who did it
EIKP/EIPO - foreign trade header and item data
oracle: GTM screening/compliance result tables [Fusion Global Trade]

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: For every export goods issue, retrieve the screening result in force at that timestamp and test both its existence and its currency against policy.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Screening_Performed, Screening_Expiry, Compliance_Block_Released and Goods_Issue to expose shipments that moved outside a valid screening window.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT l.VBELN, l.WADAT_IST, s.screen_date, s.valid_until, h.released_by
FROM LIKP l JOIN export_orders e USING(VBELN)
LEFT JOIN screening s USING(KUNNR) LEFT JOIN block_release h USING(VBELN)
WHERE s.screen_date IS NULL OR l.WADAT_IST > s.valid_until -> flag Screening_Breach

branchingDAG.hitl: Trade Compliance Lead approves retrospective screening evidence
Legal and Trade Compliance approve voluntary disclosure assessment

patterns.name: Export Document Mismatch
patterns.mentalModel: The commercial invoice, the packing list and the customs declaration all describe the same shipment, and if they disagree the shipment stops at the border — or worse, it clears and the discrepancy surfaces in a post-clearance audit two years later. Value, HS code, net weight and country of origin are the four fields that matter. I reconcile them across the document set before the truck leaves, because after that every correction is an amendment with a paper trail.

sap: EIKP/EIPO (STAWN, HERKL, EXPVZ) - commodity code, country of origin, export procedure
VBRK/VBRP (NETWR, FKIMG) - commercial invoice value and quantity
LIKP/LIPS (BTGEW, NTGEW) - gross and net weight on the delivery
/SAPSLL/ customs declaration items
oracle: Fusion Global Trade classification and declaration tables

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Assemble value, HS code, net weight and origin from the commercial invoice, the delivery and the customs declaration for the same shipment and test for field-level agreement.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Invoice_Issued, Declaration_Filed and Border_Event to expose mismatches before or after clearance.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT shipment, inv.NETWR, dec.declared_value, inv.STAWN, dec.hs_code,
       ABS(inv.NETWR - dec.declared_value) AS value_gap
FROM commercial_invoice inv JOIN customs_declaration dec USING(shipment)
WHERE inv.STAWN <> dec.hs_code OR value_gap > tolerance -> flag Doc_Mismatch

branchingDAG.hitl: Trade Compliance Lead approves reclassification and refiling
Legal and Trade Compliance approve voluntary customs amendment

patterns.name: Confirmation Optimism
patterns.mentalModel: ATP will happily confirm a date against a planned receipt, and a planned receipt is an opinion. If a plant's inbound consistently lands four days after its planned date, every confirmation resting on that receipt is already late at the moment it is given. I score confirmations by what they lean on — free stock, firm receipt or planned receipt — and I weight the planned-receipt ones by that plant and material's historic receipt reliability. The customer does not care that the confirmation was arithmetically correct.

sap: VBEP (EDATU, BMENG, WMENG) - schedule line confirmed date and quantity
MDVM / MD04 elements - the receipt element ATP confirmed against
EKET (EINDT, SLFDT) - purchase order planned vs statistical delivery date
MSEG (BUDAT, BWART=101) - when the receipt actually posted
oracle: MTL_SUPPLY (SUPPLY_TYPE_CODE, EXPECTED_DELIVERY_DATE) [Fusion] - supply ATP leaned on

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Attribute each confirmed schedule line to the supply element ATP used, then join that element class to its historic plan-versus-actual receipt variance for the plant and material.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Confirmation_Given, Supply_Element_Planned_Date and Supply_Actual_Receipt to expose confirmations built on habitually late supply.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT p.WERKS, p.MATNR, s.supply_class,
       AVG(actual_receipt - planned_receipt) AS mean_slip, COUNT(*) AS confirmations
FROM VBEP v JOIN supply_element s USING(line) JOIN receipts r USING(element)
WHERE s.supply_class = 'planned' GROUP BY 1,2,3
HAVING mean_slip >= 2 -> flag Optimistic_Confirmation

branchingDAG.condition: ELSE IF Mean_Slip >= 3 days AND At_Risk_Volume >= 100K
branchingDAG.hitl: Order Management Operations Lead approves reliability-adjusted confirmation
Customer Compliance Lead approves expedite or substitution

patterns.name: Allocation Hoarding
patterns.mentalModel: When stock is short and allocation is by order book, the rational thing for a market to do is order more than it needs. Then, once allocation is locked, the tail quietly cancels. The result is that constrained stock sat reserved against demand that never existed while a market that ordered honestly went short. I compare ordered quantity at allocation lock to shipped quantity, per market and material, across allocation cycles — the ones with a persistent cancellation tail are gaming the mechanism.

sap: VBAP (KWMENG, ABGRU) - ordered quantity and rejection reason
Allocation / product-allocation tables (planned allocation quantity per period)
LIPS (LFIMG) - what actually shipped
CDPOS (VBAP, FNAME='KWMENG') - post-allocation quantity reductions

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Snapshot ordered quantity at the allocation lock date per market and material, then difference it against shipped quantity and post-lock cancellations.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Allocation_Lock, Post_Lock_Reduction and Shipment events across cycles to expose a repeating cancellation tail.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT market, MATNR, cycle,
       SUM(qty_at_lock) AS claimed, SUM(shipped) AS taken,
       1 - SUM(shipped)/NULLIF(SUM(qty_at_lock),0) AS tail
FROM allocation_snapshot JOIN shipments USING(line)
GROUP BY 1,2,3 HAVING tail >= 0.2 AND cycles_with_tail >= 3 -> flag Hoarding

branchingDAG.hitl: Order Management Operations Lead approves allocation haircut
Commercial Finance approves allocation rebalance across markets

patterns.name: Unconsented Substitution
patterns.mentalModel: Substituting a material to protect fill rate is fine when the customer has agreed to it and catastrophic when they have not. The fill-rate report counts the substitute as a hit; the customer counts it as a miss and short-pays. I test every substitution for a recorded consent flag or a standing substitution agreement, and I treat consent-less substitutions as future deductions rather than as service saves.

sap: VBAP (MATNR, UEPOS) - ordered versus delivered material on the line
LIPS (MATNR, LFIMG) - what was actually picked
KNMT (customer material info record) - agreed substitution set
VBAK (BSTNK) - the customer PO the substitution deviates from

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Compare ordered to delivered material per line, and test the pair against the customer's approved substitution set and any recorded consent event.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Substitution_Applied, Consent_Recorded and Deduction_Received to expose substitutions that convert into short-pays.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT a.KUNNR, a.MATNR AS ordered, p.MATNR AS shipped, COUNT(*) AS subs,
       SUM(CASE WHEN d.deduction_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS became_deduction
FROM VBAP a JOIN LIPS p USING(VBELN,POSNR)
LEFT JOIN KNMT k ON k.KUNNR=a.KUNNR AND k.MATNR=p.MATNR
LEFT JOIN deductions d USING(VBELN)
WHERE a.MATNR <> p.MATNR AND k.MATNR IS NULL -> flag Unconsented

branchingDAG.hitl: Order Management Operations Lead approves shipment without prior consent
Disputes & Deductions Lead approves substitution block for this customer

patterns.name: Plan-to-Actual Route Drift
patterns.mentalModel: A route plan is built to a sequence and a time window. What actually happens is a driver's own order of work, which is usually shorter for them and longer for us. Drops per day looks acceptable while the plan quietly stops being followed. I compare planned stop sequence and window to the executed timestamps and measure adherence per route and per driver — persistent drift means the plan is wrong or the plan is ignored, and those need different fixes.

sap: /DSD/HH_ROUTE - planned route, stop sequence and time windows
/DSD/HH_VISIT - executed visit timestamps and sequence
LIKP (WADAT_IST) - goods issue per stop
TVRO / route master - planned service time per stop
oracle: Oracle Field Service activity and route tables - planned versus actual sequence

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Align planned stop sequence and window against executed visit timestamps per route-day, and compute sequence adherence and window adherence separately.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Planned_Stop, Actual_Arrival and Departure events to expose systematic resequencing and window breaches.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT route, driver, day,
       kendall_tau(planned_seq, actual_seq) AS sequence_adherence,
       AVG(CASE WHEN actual_arrival BETWEEN win_start AND win_end THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS window_adherence
FROM planned_stops JOIN actual_visits USING(route, day, stop)
GROUP BY 1,2,3 HAVING sequence_adherence < 0.6 -> flag Route_Drift

branchingDAG.hitl: DSD Field Operations Lead approves driver coaching action
DSD Route Planning Lead approves route rebuild

patterns.name: Phantom Call Compliance
patterns.mentalModel: Call compliance is measured by whether the stop was marked visited. That is a button, not a visit. The tell is dwell time and geofence: a store marked served in ninety seconds, or marked served from two kilometres away, did not get served. I score every visit on dwell, distance and whether any transaction resulted, and I look at the driver-level distribution rather than the individual stop, because one bad stop is a bad day and a pattern is something else.

sap: /DSD/HH_VISIT (visit start, visit end, status) - dwell time per call
/DSD/HH_ROUTE - the stop that was meant to be served
VBAK / LIKP - whether an order or delivery resulted from the call
Mobile device GPS capture tables - geofence position at confirmation
oracle: Oracle Field Service activity records (start, end, coordinates)

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: For each confirmed visit compute dwell time, distance between confirmation position and store geocode, and whether any order or delivery document resulted.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Visit_Start, Visit_End, Position_Fix and Transaction_Created to expose confirmations without a plausible service event.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT driver, COUNT(*) AS calls,
       SUM(CASE WHEN dwell_sec < 120 OR geo_distance_m > 500 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS implausible,
       SUM(CASE WHEN txn_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_transaction
FROM visits GROUP BY 1
HAVING implausible / calls >= 0.15 -> flag Phantom_Calls

branchingDAG.hitl: DSD Field Operations Lead approves supervisor ride-along
Internal Audit approves route settlement freeze and investigation

patterns.name: Sub-Economic Stop Persistence
patterns.mentalModel: Every route carries stops that stopped paying their way two years ago. They persist because removing a customer is a conversation nobody wants and because the route plan is inherited rather than rebuilt. I cost each stop properly — service time, drive time, drop cost — and compare it to trailing revenue and margin. A stop below cost to serve is not automatically a stop to drop; it is a stop that needs a different frequency, a different channel, or a minimum order.

sap: /DSD/HH_VISIT - service time actually consumed per stop
VBRP (NETWR, FKIMG) - trailing revenue per ship-to
TVRO / route master - drive time and drop cost assumptions
KNVV (KUNNR, VKORG) - customer sales area and price group
oracle: Field Service activity duration per stop
RA_CUSTOMER_TRX_LINES_ALL - trailing revenue by ship-to site

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Allocate service, drive and drop cost to each stop and compare to trailing twelve-month margin for that ship-to.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Monthly_Stop_Margin and Cost_To_Serve to expose stops that crossed below breakeven and stayed there.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT ship_to, route,
       SUM(margin_12m) AS margin, SUM(service_cost + drive_cost + drop_cost) AS cost_to_serve
FROM stop_economics GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING margin < cost_to_serve AND months_below_breakeven >= 6 -> flag Sub_Economic

branchingDAG.hitl: DSD Route Planning Lead approves call-frequency change
Sales Operations approves channel migration or minimum order proposal

patterns.name: End-of-Shift Batch Confirmation
patterns.mentalModel: When eleven deliveries are all confirmed within four minutes at the end of a shift, they were not confirmed as they happened — they were keyed in the cab at the depot. Every timestamp downstream is then fiction: proof of delivery times, temperature compliance windows, service-level evidence. I look at the inter-confirmation interval distribution per route-day; real execution is spread, back-entry is a spike.

sap: /DSD/HH_VISIT - confirmation timestamps per stop
LIKP (WADAT_IST, ERZET) - goods issue date and entry time
/DSD/SL_SETTLE - settlement record for the shift
Mobile sync log - when the device actually transmitted

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Order confirmation timestamps within each route-day and compute the distribution of intervals between consecutive confirmations, plus the gap between confirmation and device transmission.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Stop_Confirmations across the shift to expose clusters inconsistent with physical travel time between stops.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT route, day, COUNT(*) AS stops,
       SUM(CASE WHEN interval_sec < 120 AND drive_time_required > 600 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS impossible
FROM confirmations GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING impossible >= 3 -> flag Batch_Confirmation

branchingDAG.hitl: DSD Field Operations Lead approves SLA evidence restatement
Quality and Compliance approve cold-chain evidence review

patterns.name: Distributor Reporting Opacity
patterns.mentalModel: Distributor-operated routes report to me in aggregates — cases delivered, invoices raised — while own-fleet routes report every exception at store and SKU level. So distributor performance always looks better, because the failures never reach my report. I measure reporting granularity itself: the ratio of exception records to drops. When a distributor reports a tenth of the exceptions per drop that own fleet does, the difference is visibility, not performance.

sap: /DSD/HH_VISIT - exception records by route and operator type
LIKP / LIPS - delivery and item level detail received per route
LFA1 / KNA1 - distributor master and operating model flag
VBRK - invoices raised against distributor routes

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Compute exception records per hundred drops separately for own-fleet and distributor routes, controlling for territory and product mix.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Drop_Executed and Exception_Reported by operator type to expose systematically absent exception reporting.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT operator_type, distributor, COUNT(exception_id)*100.0/COUNT(DISTINCT drop_id) AS exc_per_100
FROM drops LEFT JOIN exceptions USING(drop_id)
GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING operator_type='distributor' AND exc_per_100 < 0.25 * own_fleet_benchmark
  -> flag Reporting_Opacity

branchingDAG.hitl: DSD Field Operations Lead approves reporting requirement change
Commercial Finance approves distributor performance audit

patterns.name: Repeat Failed Delivery Loop
patterns.mentalModel: The same store fails on the same reason week after week — no access before ten, no purchase order on file, wrong delivery window — and every week we send a truck anyway. Each individual failure gets closed as an exception. Nobody fixes the master data behind it. I group failed deliveries by store and reason code and count repeats; anything failing three times on one reason is a data defect wearing an operations costume.

sap: LIKP (VBELN, LFDAT) + delivery blocking/failure reason codes
/DSD/HH_VISIT - failed call reason at the stop
KNVV / KNA1 (delivery window, unloading point) - the master data behind the failure
TVLS / delivery status tables

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Group failed deliveries by ship-to and reason code, count repeats within a rolling window, and join the master data field the reason implicates.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Failure_Events per store and reason to expose repeats that no master-data change ever followed.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT ship_to, reason_code, COUNT(*) AS failures,
       MAX(master_data_last_changed) AS last_fix
FROM failed_deliveries GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING failures >= 3 AND last_fix < MIN(failure_date) -> flag Unremediated_Loop

branchingDAG.hitl: OTC Master Data Lead approves master data change
Sales Operations approves suspension of scheduled deliveries

patterns.name: Cash Banking Lag
patterns.mentalModel: In van sales the driver holds company cash from the moment of the first collection to the moment it hits the bank. Every hour of that is float and every day of it is risk. Settlement records tell me when cash was declared; the bank statement tells me when it arrived. The gap between those two, per driver, is the number I care about — and a gap that widens at month end, or for one driver only, is not a logistics problem.

sap: /DSD/SL_SETTLE - declared cash at route settlement
FEBKO/FEBEP - bank statement line items and value dates
BSEG (HKONT cash-in-transit) - the clearing account the float sits in
/DSD/HH_VISIT - time of first cash collection on the route

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Match declared route cash to its bank credit and compute the elapsed time from first collection to bank value date, per driver and route.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence First_Collection, Settlement_Declared and Bank_Value_Date to expose float held beyond policy.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT driver, route, settle_date,
       bank_value_date - first_collection_time AS float_hours, declared_cash
FROM route_settlement JOIN bank_credit USING(settlement_ref)
WHERE float_hours > policy_hours -> flag Banking_Lag

branchingDAG.hitl: DSD Settlement Office Lead approves route clearance hold
Internal Audit approves suspension of cash-handling authority

patterns.name: Load-to-Settle Shrinkage
patterns.mentalModel: Stock loaded must equal stock sold plus stock returned plus stock accounted as damaged. When it does not, the difference walked off the truck. Individually these are a case here and a case there, well inside anyone's tolerance. Aggregated by driver over a quarter they are a number worth acting on. I reconcile every route on a strict three-way basis and I trend the residual per driver rather than judging any single day.

sap: MSEG (BWART 601/602, MENGE) - goods issue and return movements per route
/DSD/SL_SETTLE - declared sales, returns and damages at settlement
MSKU / special stock at driver or vehicle
LIPS (LFIMG) - delivered quantity confirmed at stops

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Build a three-way reconciliation per route-day of loaded, sold, returned and damaged quantities, and carry the unexplained residual to the driver.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Load, Sale, Return and Settlement events to expose a persistent unexplained residual by driver over time.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT driver, period,
       SUM(loaded - sold - returned - damaged) AS residual_cases,
       SUM((loaded - sold - returned - damaged) * std_cost) AS residual_value
FROM route_reconciliation GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING residual_value >= threshold AND periods_positive >= 3 -> flag Shrinkage

branchingDAG.hitl: DSD Settlement Office Lead approves unannounced vehicle stock count
Internal Audit approves loss investigation

patterns.name: Settlement Credit Note Spike
patterns.mentalModel: When a route will not settle, the fastest way to make it settle is a credit note. Raised at the point of settlement, for a round number, against a customer who never asked for it — that credit is squaring a cash or stock variance, not correcting a billing error. I watch credit notes raised inside the settlement window by the settling user, and I compare their reason-code mix to credits raised through the normal billing correction route.

sap: VBRK (FKART='G2', ERDAT, ERZET, ERNAM) - credit memo header, who and when
/DSD/SL_SETTLE - settlement window timestamps for the route
VBRP (NETWR) - credit value and the invoice it references
Credit memo reason codes (AUGRU)

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Select credit memos created within the route settlement window by the settling user and compare volume, value roundness and reason-code mix against the baseline correction population.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Settlement_Opened, Credit_Note_Raised and Settlement_Cleared to expose credits that exist only to close a variance.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT route, settling_user, COUNT(*) AS credits, SUM(NETWR) AS value,
       AVG(CASE WHEN MOD(NETWR,100)=0 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS round_ratio
FROM VBRK c JOIN settlement s ON c.ERDAT BETWEEN s.open AND s.close
WHERE c.FKART='G2' GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING credits >= 3 AND round_ratio > 0.6 -> flag Settlement_Credits

branchingDAG.hitl: DSD Settlement Office Lead approves credit reversal and settlement reopen
OTC Controls Lead approves removal of credit-note authority

patterns.name: Empties Return Divergence
patterns.mentalModel: Crates, kegs and pallets are company assets on loan, and the loop only closes if what goes out comes back. Per drop the divergence is trivial; per customer per year it is a fleet of pallets. I track issued against returned by customer and route, age the open balance, and reconcile it to the deposit liability we carry. A customer whose open balance only ever grows is either losing our assets or selling them.

sap: MSKU (special stock with customer - returnable packaging balance)
MSEG (BWART 601/602 with returnable packaging material) - issue and return movements
/DSD/SL_SETTLE - empties declared at route settlement
BSEG - deposit liability carried per customer
oracle: MTL_MATERIAL_TRANSACTIONS - issue and return of returnable items

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Net issued against returned returnable units per customer and route, age the open balance, and reconcile it to the carried deposit liability.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Asset_Issued, Asset_Returned and Balance_Aged to expose customers whose open balance never reduces.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT KUNNR, material, SUM(issued - returned) AS open_units,
       AVG(days_open) AS avg_age, open_units * unit_cost AS float_value
FROM returnable_movements GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING open_units > threshold AND trend(open_units) > 0 -> flag Return_Divergence

branchingDAG.hitl: Returnable Assets Manager approves deposit billing enforcement
Credit & Collections approve asset loss charge and issue suspension

patterns.name: Unauthorised Return Receipt
patterns.mentalModel: Goods come back on a pallet with a handwritten note and the warehouse books them in, because refusing a delivery is a fight nobody at the dock wants. From that moment the return has no authorisation, no reason code and no root cause — and a credit will follow because the stock is on our books. I match every return receipt to an RMA that existed before the goods arrived, and I treat the unmatched ones as a control failure at the dock rather than a paperwork problem in the office.

sap: VBAK (AUART='RE', ERDAT) - the return order and when it was raised
LIKP / LIPS (returns delivery) - the physical receipt
MSEG (BWART 651/653, BUDAT) - the goods movement back into stock
VBRK (FKART='G2') - the credit that follows

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Join every return goods movement to a return order and compare the return order creation date to the receipt posting date, flagging receipts with no prior authorisation.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence RMA_Created, Goods_Received and Credit_Issued to expose receipts that preceded their own authorisation or had none.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT m.WERKS, m.KUNNR, COUNT(*) AS receipts,
       SUM(CASE WHEN r.VBELN IS NULL OR r.ERDAT > m.BUDAT THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS unauthorised
FROM MSEG m LEFT JOIN VBAK r ON r.VBELN = m.return_ref AND r.AUART = 'RE'
WHERE m.BWART IN ('651','653') GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING unauthorised * 1.0 / receipts >= 0.1 -> flag Unauthorised_Returns

branchingDAG.hitl: Returns & Claims Lead approves retrospective return authorisation
Global Process Owner approves dock refusal control

patterns.name: Disposition Default Drift
patterns.mentalModel: Scrap is the fastest disposition. It needs no inspection, no relabelling, no decision — so under pressure it becomes the default, and salvage recovery quietly collapses. The give-away is disposition mix moving while return reason mix stays flat: the goods coming back have not changed, only what we decide to do with them. I trend disposition by reason code and by who made the call, and I recompute the recovery we forfeited at the resaleable value we could have realised.

sap: MSEG (BWART 653/655/551, MENGE) - return to unrestricted, to blocked, or to scrap
QMEL / QMFE (quality notification and defect code) - the inspection result
VBAP (AUGRU) - return reason code on the return order
MBEW (VERPR, STPRS) - the value forfeited on scrap

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Cross-tabulate return reason code against disposition movement type by period and inspector, and value the difference between scrap and resaleable disposition.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Return_Reason_Recorded, Inspection_Result and Disposition_Posted to expose scrap decisions taken without an inspection supporting them.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT period, inspector, reason_code,
       SUM(CASE WHEN disposition='scrap' THEN qty END)*1.0/SUM(qty) AS scrap_share,
       SUM(CASE WHEN disposition='scrap' AND inspection_id IS NULL THEN qty*std_cost END) AS forfeited
FROM return_dispositions GROUP BY 1,2,3
HAVING scrap_share > baseline_scrap_share * 1.5 -> flag Disposition_Drift

branchingDAG.hitl: Returns & Claims Lead approves mandatory pre-scrap inspection
OTC Controls Lead approves scrap authority suspension

patterns.name: Credit Ahead of Receipt
patterns.mentalModel: A customer says the goods are coming back and asks for the credit now. Someone helpful raises it. Then the goods do not arrive, or arrive short, or arrive damaged in a way that would have changed the credit — and the money is already gone. I never let the credit lead the receipt without a documented decision. Every credit raised against a return order with no corresponding goods movement after a reasonable window is an open recovery, not a closed case.

sap: VBRK (FKART='G2', FKDAT) - credit memo and its date
VBFA - document flow from return order to credit and to goods movement
MSEG (BWART 651/653, BUDAT) - whether the stock ever came back
VBAP (KWMENG) versus LIPS (LFIMG) - authorised versus received quantity

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: For each return credit, look for a goods receipt against the same return order and compare quantity and timing; age credits with no receipt beyond the agreed return window.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Credit_Issued, Expected_Return_Window and Goods_Receipt to expose credits that were never earned.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT c.VBELN AS credit, c.FKDAT, r.VBELN AS rma, SUM(m.MENGE) AS received,
       c.credit_qty, DATEDIFF(today, c.FKDAT) AS age_days
FROM VBRK c JOIN VBFA f ON f.VBELN = c.VBELN
LEFT JOIN MSEG m ON m.return_ref = f.VBELV
GROUP BY 1,2,3,5 HAVING COALESCE(received,0) < c.credit_qty AND age_days > return_window
  -> flag Credit_Ahead_Of_Receipt

branchingDAG.condition: ELSE IF No_Receipt AND Age > Window AND Value >= 10K
branchingDAG.hitl: Returns & Claims Lead approves credit reversal
Credit & Collections approve customer-level credit-before-receipt block

patterns.name: Concentrated Return Source
patterns.mentalModel: Returns get managed as a customer behaviour problem when most of the volume is usually a product problem wearing a customer's name. When one SKU, one batch or one pack format accounts for a disproportionate share of returns across unrelated customers, that is not a returns issue — it is quality or specification, and it will keep costing until somebody upstream owns it. I decompose returns by SKU, batch and customer and test whether concentration sits on the product axis or the customer axis before assigning the problem.

sap: VBAP (MATNR, CHARG, AUGRU) - returned material, batch and reason
VBRP (FKIMG, NETWR) - original sales volume as the denominator
QMEL (defect code, MATNR) - quality notifications raised
MCHB / batch master - production batch and plant of origin

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Compute return rate per SKU, per batch and per customer against matched sales volume, then compare concentration on the product axis to concentration on the customer axis.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Batch_Produced, Sold and Returned to expose returns clustering on a production window rather than a buyer.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT MATNR, CHARG, COUNT(DISTINCT KUNNR) AS customers,
       SUM(returned_qty)*1.0/NULLIF(SUM(sold_qty),0) AS return_rate
FROM returns_vs_sales GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING return_rate > 3 * category_baseline AND customers >= 5 -> flag Product_Axis_Concentration

branchingDAG.hitl: Quality approves batch quarantine and containment
Global Process Owner approves specification review and cost reassignment

patterns.name: Silent Field Decay
patterns.mentalModel: Customer masters are created under a governed workflow and then edited freely for the next ten years. The fields that matter most downstream — payment terms, dunning procedure, tax classification, incoterm, credit control area — are exactly the ones a single change can move without anyone approving it. I read the change log rather than the master record: who changed which controlled field, when, and whether any request or approval sat behind it. A controlled field changed outside workflow is a defect regardless of whether the new value is right.

sap: CDHDR/CDPOS (OBJECTCLAS='DEBI', FNAME, USERNAME, UDATE) - customer master change log
KNB1 (ZTERM, MAHNA) - payment terms and dunning procedure
KNVV (INCO1, KTGRD, VKORG) - sales-area controlled fields
SWWWIHEAD - the governance workflow instance, where one exists

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Filter change documents to the controlled field list, join each change to a governance workflow instance, and flag changes with no approving instance.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Change_Request, Approval and Field_Change to expose changes where the field moved without the first two.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT c.FNAME, c.USERNAME, COUNT(*) AS changes,
       SUM(CASE WHEN w.workflow_id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS ungoverned
FROM CDPOS c LEFT JOIN workflow w ON w.object_key = c.OBJECTID AND w.field = c.FNAME
WHERE c.OBJECTCLAS='DEBI' AND c.FNAME IN (controlled_fields)
GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING ungoverned > 0 -> flag Silent_Change

branchingDAG.hitl: OTC Master Data Lead approves field revert and retrospective request
OTC Controls Lead approves removal of direct maintenance authority

patterns.name: Emergency Create Backlog
patterns.mentalModel: Every master data process has an emergency path, because sometimes an order genuinely cannot wait. The deal is that the record gets created now and validated within a few days. In practice the validation queue is where good intentions go to die, and a year later a third of the customer base was created on the fast path and never checked. I age every emergency-created record by time since creation without completion, because an emergency that is ninety days old was never an emergency.

sap: KNA1 (ERDAT, ERNAM) + creation route flag or transaction code from CDHDR
CDHDR (TCODE) - whether created via the governed path or directly
KNB1/KNVV completeness - mandatory fields still blank
VBAK - transactions already booked against the incomplete record
oracle: OE_ORDER_HEADERS_ALL - orders taken against provisional accounts

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Identify records created through the emergency route, test mandatory field completeness, and age those still incomplete against the policy validation window.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Emergency_Create, Validation_Due and Validation_Completed to expose records that never returned for completion.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT k.KUNNR, k.ERDAT, k.ERNAM, DATEDIFF(today, k.ERDAT) AS age_days,
       missing_mandatory_fields, order_value_since_create
FROM KNA1 k JOIN creation_route r USING(KUNNR)
WHERE r.route = 'emergency' AND missing_mandatory_fields > 0
  AND age_days > policy_days -> flag Stale_Emergency_Record

branchingDAG.condition: ELSE IF Age > 30 days AND Transactions_Booked >= 50K
branchingDAG.hitl: OTC Master Data Lead approves provisional flag and completion task

branchingDAG.condition: ELSE IF Age > 90 days OR Emergency_Route_Share > 25%
branchingDAG.hitl: Global Process Owner approves order block and emergency-route review

patterns.name: Stale Tax Classification
patterns.mentalModel: Tax classification and commodity codes are set once and then the law moves. A rate change, a reclassification, a new place-of-supply rule — and every invoice after that date carries the wrong tax while looking entirely normal. Nobody notices until an audit, and by then it is thousands of documents. I compare the effective date of each regulatory change against the last change date of the classification fields it affects, per country and material group, and I treat any classification older than the rule that governs it as an open exposure.

sap: MLAN (TAXM1, ALAND) - material tax classification by country
KNVI (TAXKD) - customer tax classification
MARC/MARA (STAWN) - commodity code for the material
A003 / condition records for tax, with validity
oracle: ZX_LINES - tax actually applied on the transaction

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Join classification fields to the regulatory change calendar by country and product group and compare last-changed dates to each rule's effective date.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Regulation_Effective, Classification_Last_Changed and Invoices_Issued to size the population billed under a stale classification.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT country, product_group, rule_effective_date, MAX(classification_changed) AS last_change,
       COUNT(inv.VBELN) AS invoices_after, SUM(inv.tax_amount) AS tax_at_risk
FROM classification c JOIN regulation r USING(country, product_group)
JOIN invoices inv ON inv.FKDAT >= r.rule_effective_date
GROUP BY 1,2,3 HAVING last_change < rule_effective_date -> flag Stale_Classification

branchingDAG.condition: ELSE IF Stale AND Tax_At_Risk >= 25K AND Under_Charged
branchingDAG.hitl: Tax approves classification correction and exposure assessment
Tax and Legal approve filing amendment and customer credits

patterns.name: Partner Mapping Decay
patterns.mentalModel: EDI works until the partner upgrades their ERP, and then one segment starts arriving in a format the map was never told about. It does not fail loudly — a subset of orders fall to error, someone rekeys them manually, and the error rate creeps up while everyone assumes it is normal noise. I trend IDoc failure rate per partner per segment and look for the step change, because the date of the step change is the date of their upgrade and that is the conversation to have.

sap: EDIDC (MESTYP, SNDPRN, STATUS, CREDAT) - IDoc control record per partner
EDIDS (STATUS, STAPA1, STAMID) - status and error message detail
EDID4 (SEGNAM) - the segment that failed
VBAK (BSTNK) - the order that had to be rekeyed manually

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Aggregate inbound document failures by partner, message type and failing segment per day, and run change-point detection on the failure rate series.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Inbound_Received, Segment_Error and Manual_Rekey events to expose a step change in one partner's failure profile.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT SNDPRN, MESTYP, SEGNAM, day,
       failures*1.0/NULLIF(received,0) AS fail_rate,
       changepoint(fail_rate) AS break_date
FROM edi_daily GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
HAVING fail_rate > 0.05 AND break_date IS NOT NULL -> flag Mapping_Decay

branchingDAG.hitl: Digital Channel Integration Lead approves map change and reprocessing
Global Process Owner approves partner change-control escalation

patterns.name: Unreturned Acknowledgement
patterns.mentalModel: The dangerous EDI failure is not the one that errors — it is the one where we accept the order, never send the acknowledgement, and both sides believe something different. The customer thinks it is confirmed. We may have rejected a line. Nobody finds out until the delivery is short and the chargeback arrives. I reconcile inbound orders against outbound acknowledgements within the agreed SLA and treat a missing acknowledgement as an open commitment, not a technical backlog item.

sap: EDIDC (MESTYP='ORDERS' inbound versus 'ORDRSP' outbound, SNDPRN/RCVPRN)
EDIDS - dispatch status of the outbound acknowledgement
VBAK (VBELN, BSTNK) - the order created from the inbound message
VBAP (ABGRU) - lines rejected that the customer was never told about
oracle: ECX_DOCLOGS - inbound and outbound document pairing

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Pair each inbound order document with its outbound acknowledgement by partner and reference, and measure elapsed time against the partner SLA, flagging unpaired inbound documents.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Order_Received, Order_Created, Line_Rejected and Acknowledgement_Sent to expose commitments the customer was never told about.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT i.SNDPRN, i.DOCNUM, o.DOCNUM AS ack, i.CREDAT,
       DATEDIFF(hour, i.CREDAT, o.CREDAT) AS ack_hours, v.rejected_lines
FROM edi_in i LEFT JOIN edi_out o ON o.ref = i.DOCNUM
JOIN VBAK v ON v.BSTNK = i.po_number
WHERE o.DOCNUM IS NULL OR ack_hours > sla_hours -> flag Ack_Gap

branchingDAG.hitl: Digital Channel Integration Lead approves corrective acknowledgement
Customer Compliance Lead approves pre-emptive customer contact

patterns.name: Channel Price Divergence
patterns.mentalModel: The webshop caches prices. The portal has its own catalogue. EDI prices from the partner's copy of our price file. Each of those is a place where the price a customer sees can differ from the condition record that will actually invoice them — and the customer will short-pay to the price they were shown, every time, and they will be right to. I reconcile the price presented on each digital channel against the ERP condition record for the same customer and material, and I fix the channel before the deduction arrives.

sap: KONP / KONH - the authoritative condition record and its validity
Channel catalogue and price file extracts per digital channel
VBAP (NETWR, KBETR) - the price the order was actually created at
BSEG / dispute records - short-pays citing price
oracle: Commerce catalogue price tables / channel cache

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Compare the price published on each channel to the ERP condition record for the same customer, material and date, and join to any resulting short-pay.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Price_Changed_In_ERP, Channel_Refresh and Order_Placed to expose the window in which the channel was serving a stale price.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT channel, KUNNR, MATNR, channel_price, erp_price,
       channel_price - erp_price AS delta, orders_in_window
FROM channel_catalogue c JOIN erp_conditions e USING(KUNNR, MATNR, valid_on)
WHERE ABS(channel_price - erp_price) > tolerance -> flag Channel_Divergence

branchingDAG.hitl: Digital Channel Integration Lead approves honouring published price
Commercial Finance approves proactive customer credit

patterns.name: Benefit Double Count
patterns.mentalModel: Two workstreams, two markets, one saving. The automation programme claims the headcount, the process programme claims the same headcount under a different name, and the business case adds up to more than the P&L will ever show. Benefits realisation only means something if every claim traces to a distinct, measurable ledger movement. I reconcile claimed benefits to their underlying cost centre or KPI baseline and look for the same baseline claimed twice.

sap: CSKS / cost centre master and COSP actuals - the ledger the saving must appear in
PROJ / PRPS - the programme and work breakdown claiming it
Benefit register (claim, baseline reference, owner, value)
GLPCA / ACDOCA - the actual movement against the baseline

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Resolve each benefit claim to the cost centre, KPI and baseline period it rests on, then group claims by that triple and flag any triple claimed by more than one workstream.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Baseline_Set, Claim_Registered and Ledger_Movement to expose claims sharing a baseline or unsupported by any movement.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT cost_centre, kpi, baseline_period,
       COUNT(DISTINCT workstream) AS claimants, SUM(claimed_value) AS claimed,
       MAX(actual_ledger_delta) AS realised
FROM benefit_register GROUP BY 1,2,3
HAVING claimants > 1 OR claimed > realised * 1.2 -> flag Double_Count

branchingDAG.hitl: Transformation PMO Lead approves benefit netting and restatement
Financial Controller approves benefits restatement

patterns.name: Post-Go-Live Adoption Decay
patterns.mentalModel: Adoption is measured in the four weeks after go-live, when hypercare is watching and everybody is on best behaviour. Then the support team leaves and the old habits return — the manual spreadsheet, the direct transaction, the workaround that was always faster. The benefit was booked on week-four adoption. I measure the transaction mix continuously and look for the reversion curve, because a benefit that decays is a benefit we are still reporting and no longer earning.

sap: STAD / SM20 or equivalent usage statistics by transaction and user
VBAK (VBTYP, ORDER_SOURCE) - orders arriving via the new path versus the legacy path
CDHDR (TCODE) - which transaction actually created the document
Benefit register - the adoption assumption the benefit rests on
oracle: FND_LOGIN / audit of responsibility and page usage [Fusion]

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Measure the share of transactions executed through the target process path per market per week and compare the current share to the hypercare-exit share the benefit assumed.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Go_Live, Hypercare_Exit and Weekly_Adoption_Share to expose reversion after support withdrawal.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT market, week, target_path_txns*1.0/NULLIF(total_txns,0) AS adoption,
       adoption - adoption_at_hypercare_exit AS drift
FROM process_usage GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING drift <= -0.15 AND weeks_since_golive >= 8 -> flag Adoption_Decay

branchingDAG.hitl: Transformation PMO Lead approves benefit revaluation
Global Process Owner approves legacy path closure

patterns.name: Silent Scope Descope
patterns.mentalModel: Waves hit their dates because scope quietly leaves them. A country drops out, a process variant is deferred, an interface is postponed to a later phase that never gets funded — and the date is met, the status stays green, and the business case is never re-baselined against what actually shipped. I reconcile delivered scope to committed scope wave by wave and revalue the benefit on what was actually deployed, not what was planned.

sap: PROJ / PRPS - work breakdown and its status by wave
Deployment scope register (markets, processes, interfaces committed per wave)
Transaction evidence per market - whether the process is actually running there
Benefit register - benefit attributed to each scope item
oracle: PJF_PROJECTS_ALL_B / PJF_TASKS_V - wave and task structure

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Compare committed scope items per wave to those with live transaction evidence after go-live, and re-attribute benefit to delivered scope only.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Scope_Committed, Scope_Changed and First_Live_Transaction to expose items that left scope without a benefit re-baseline.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT wave, scope_item, committed_flag, live_evidence_flag, benefit_attributed,
       rebaselined_flag
FROM scope_register LEFT JOIN transaction_evidence USING(scope_item)
WHERE committed_flag = 1 AND live_evidence_flag = 0 AND rebaselined_flag = 0
  -> flag Silent_Descope

branchingDAG.hitl: Transformation PMO Lead approves business case re-baseline
Financial Controller approves steering committee disclosure

patterns.name: Deposit Liability Drift
patterns.mentalModel: Three numbers have to agree: the units physically in the field, the deposits we have billed, and the deposit liability carried on the balance sheet. In practice they are maintained by three different teams and reconciled by nobody. Deposits get billed on issue but never released on return, or released twice, and the liability slowly detaches from reality. I reconcile all three monthly and treat the residual as an audit finding in waiting, because that is what it becomes.

sap: MSKU (KUNNR, MATNR, KULAB) - returnable stock physically held at each customer
BSEG (HKONT deposit liability, DMBTR) - the liability carried in the ledger
VBRP (KSCHL deposit condition) - deposits billed and released on invoices and credits
MSEG (BWART 601/602 on returnable packaging) - the movements behind both

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Value physical customer-held units at the deposit rate, sum net deposits billed less released per customer, and difference both against the carried ledger liability.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Asset_Issued, Deposit_Billed, Asset_Returned and Deposit_Released to expose the leg that stops firing.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT KUNNR, SUM(KULAB * deposit_rate) AS physical_value,
       SUM(deposit_billed - deposit_released) AS net_billed,
       MAX(ledger_liability) AS carried,
       SUM(KULAB * deposit_rate) - MAX(ledger_liability) AS residual
FROM MSKU JOIN deposits USING(KUNNR) JOIN ledger USING(KUNNR)
GROUP BY 1 HAVING ABS(residual) >= threshold -> flag Deposit_Drift

branchingDAG.hitl: Financial Controller approves deposit liability adjustment
Financial Controller approves prior-period deposit restatement

patterns.name: Depot Pool Leakage
patterns.mentalModel: Every empties loss gets charged to the customer by default, because that is the easiest party to blame and the one we can invoice. But when losses cluster on one depot or one route rather than across the customers they serve, the assets are not disappearing at the customer — they are disappearing between the customer and the yard. I test whether loss concentrates on the customer axis or the internal handling axis before anyone raises a deposit charge, because charging a customer for our own handling loss is how you lose the customer and the asset.

sap: MSEG (BWART, WERKS, LGORT) - returnable movements by plant and storage location
MSKU - the customer-held balance the loss is attributed to
/DSD/SL_SETTLE - empties declared back at route settlement
LIKP (VSTEL) - shipping point the assets left from

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Attribute every unreturned unit to both its customer and its handling chain (route, depot, shipping point), then compare concentration on each axis.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Yard_Issue, Route_Load, Customer_Delivery and Yard_Return to find the leg where units stop arriving.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT depot, route, COUNT(DISTINCT KUNNR) AS customers_affected,
       SUM(issued - returned) AS lost_units,
       lost_units / NULLIF(depot_throughput,0) AS loss_rate
FROM returnable_flow GROUP BY 1,2
HAVING loss_rate > 2 * network_baseline AND customers_affected >= 8
  -> flag Internal_Handling_Loss

branchingDAG.hitl: Returnable Assets Manager approves suspension of customer deposit charges
Internal Audit approves asset shrinkage investigation

patterns.name: Pooler Statement Divergence
patterns.mentalModel: With a third-party pallet or crate pooler we pay hire per unit per day, so every unit their system thinks we still hold costs us money whether we hold it or not. Their statement and our movement records will diverge — transfers they never posted, returns they logged late, units they show at a customer we delivered to months ago. I reconcile the pooler statement line by line against our own issue and return records and challenge the open balance, because hire accrues silently and nobody audits an invoice that arrives every month looking the same.

sap: MSEG (BWART on pooled packaging material) - our record of issues and returns
MSKU / MSLB (special stock with customer and with vendor) - pooled balances
RSEG / RBKP - the pooler's hire invoice as posted
MARA (MTART='LEIH') - returnable packaging material master
oracle: MTL_MATERIAL_TRANSACTIONS - issue and return of pooled assets [Fusion]

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Match pooler statement movements to our own goods movements on reference and date, and age the unmatched open balance the pooler is charging hire on.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Our_Issue, Our_Return, Pooler_Posted and Hire_Charged to expose units accruing hire after we returned them.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT pooler, ref, our_movement_date, pooler_posted_date,
       DATEDIFF(pooler_posted_date, our_movement_date) AS posting_lag,
       open_units * hire_rate * days_open AS hire_at_risk
FROM pooler_statement FULL OUTER JOIN our_movements USING(ref)
WHERE pooler_posted_date IS NULL OR posting_lag > tolerance_days
  -> flag Statement_Divergence

branchingDAG.hitl: Returnable Assets Manager approves withholding of disputed hire
Procurement approves joint physical audit with the pooler

patterns.name: Seasonal Float Ratchet
patterns.mentalModel: Float always grows into peak — that is expected and we plan for it. What is not expected is that it never fully unwinds afterwards. Each year the trough is a little higher than the last, and because everyone compares to the same month last year, the ratchet is invisible. I fit the trough, not the peak: if the post-peak minimum keeps rising, we are permanently funding assets that are never coming back, and buying more each season to cover it.

sap: MSKU (KULAB) - month-end customer-held balance across several years
MSEG - seasonal issue and return movement volumes
MARA / MBEW - unit cost of the returnable asset
Purchase history for replacement asset buys

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Build a multi-year monthly series of customer-held units, extract the post-peak trough each cycle, and regress trough level against cycle number.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Peak_Float, Post_Peak_Trough and Replacement_Purchase across cycles to expose a rising floor funded by new asset buys.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT cycle_year, MIN(month_end_units) AS trough,
       LAG(MIN(month_end_units)) OVER (ORDER BY cycle_year) AS prior_trough,
       SUM(replacement_purchases) AS bought
FROM float_series GROUP BY 1
HAVING trough > prior_trough * 1.05 -> flag Ratchet

branchingDAG.hitl: Returnable Assets Manager approves hold on replacement asset purchases
Financial Controller approves pool re-baseline and deposit rate change

patterns.name: Return Substitution Shortfall
patterns.mentalModel: The count reconciles and the value does not. A customer returns the right number of units but they are the cheap ones, the damaged ones, or somebody else's branded asset entirely — and because settlement counts pieces rather than grades, the loop looks closed while the good assets stay out. I reconcile returns by asset type and grade, not just quantity, and I value the mix difference. Over a year, a systematic grade downgrade on returns is worth more than most of the outright losses.

sap: MSEG (MATNR, MENGE, BWART) - the specific returnable material returned
MSKU (MATNR) - what was actually issued to that customer
MBEW (VERPR) - the value difference between grades or asset types
QMEL - damage or grading notifications on receipt

patterns.layer1_logicalMapping: Match returned asset type and grade to what was issued to the same customer and value the mix difference at standard cost.
patterns.layer2_eventSeries: Sequence Asset_Issued_By_Grade, Asset_Returned_By_Grade and Grading_Result to expose systematic downgrade on return.
patterns.conceptualSQL:
SELECT KUNNR, issued_grade, returned_grade, SUM(qty) AS units,
       SUM(qty * (issued_cost - returned_cost)) AS value_shortfall
FROM returnable_matching GROUP BY 1,2,3
HAVING issued_grade <> returned_grade AND value_shortfall >= threshold
  -> flag Grade_Substitution

branchingDAG.hitl: Returnable Assets Manager approves graded settlement and difference charge
Procurement approves rejection and inter-company asset reconciliation
